# @alexify/protoarray

> Schema-based serialization that stays JSON, for Node.js and browsers, with zero dependencies.
> Objects travel as positional JSON arrays (`{ name: 'Alex', age: 27 }` becomes `['Alex', 27]`),
> and a schema shared by the client and the server maps every position back to its key: the
> discipline of Protocol Buffers over JSON. Schemas are @alexify/metaschema's. Maintained by
> Alexis Technologies.

Key facts:
- Package (npm): `@alexify/protoarray`, installed with `npm install @alexify/protoarray
  @alexify/metaschema` (metaschema 3.4+ where schemas are defined)
- Node.js >= 18 and browsers; CommonJS with ESM named-import interop; hand-written `index.d.ts`;
  a schema is typed by the metaschema Schema it is built from (`Schema<Output, Input>`,
  `Decoded<T>`)
- Zero runtime dependencies, no build step, about 23 KB min+gzip for the core (22.7 KB the
  Node.js entry, 22.6 KB the browser one); the subpaths `/resolve`, `/registry` and `/stream` add
  1.7–2.6 KB each, `/evolve` 3.8 KB, `/standalone` 8.8 KB and `/binary` 9.1 KB. protoarray never
  requires metaschema: it recognises metaschema objects by their brand, reads snapshots as plain
  JSON, and reads a raw definition only with metaschema injected (`{ metaschema }`)
- The payload is plain JSON: about half the bytes of keyed objects before compression, and faster
  to parse and stringify (×1.5 encode, ×1.8 decode on a typical record in V8). Against
  protobufjs, protobuf-es, avsc, msgpackr, @msgpack/msgpack, cbor-x, BSON, v8.serialize,
  superjson, devalue and fast-json-stringify (https://protoarray.vercel.app/guide/benchmarks): the
  fastest encoder on records, strings and tagged messages, the fastest decoder on long strings;
  msgpackr's shared structures decode the other payloads faster; binary codecs win on mostly
  numeric payloads against the text wire. The binary wire (`/binary`) of the same schema has the
  fastest round trip of every library on all seven payloads, numeric included
- Building a schema: `Schema.from(new (require('@alexify/metaschema').Schema)('User', definition))`
  (typed); `Schema.from(definition, { metaschema: require('@alexify/metaschema') })` (or
  `@alexify/metaschema/definition`, which builds without validating); `Schema.from(snapshot)` from
  metaschema's snapshot format 1 (`schema.toSnapshot()`, `model.toJSON()`), no metaschema needed;
  `Schema.fromModel(modelOrSnapshot)` → every entity by name; `new Schema(name, source, options)`
- Definitions are written in metaschema's language (https://metaschema.vercel.app/guide/schema-syntax):
  `'string'`, `'?number'`, `'key?'`, `'integer'`, `'any'`, `'unknown'`, `'null'`, nested structs,
  `{ array: T }`, `{ set: T }`, `{ map: { K: V } }`, `{ object: { string: V } }`, `{ enum: [...] }`,
  `{ flags: [...] }`, `{ union: [...], discriminator }`, `'date'`, `'bigint'`, `'bytes'`, `'json'`,
  tuples, `{ type, required, nullable, default, decimals, aliases }`, kinds (`{ Entity: {}, … }`),
  references by name
- References travel as metaschema's check reads them: a stored kind (Entity, Registry, …) as its
  id, a memory kind (Struct) as its record; `embed` on the field or the option
  `references: 'kind' | 'embed' | 'id'` overrides; a stored kind adds a trailing optional
  `<entity>Id` field; references between schemas need a metaschema Model (a schema reaches its own
  name for recursion)
- Wire rules: one field per position in declaration order; missing/undefined/null travel as null;
  trailing nulls are trimmed; enum → index, date → epoch ms, bigint → decimal string, bytes →
  base64, decimals → scaled integer, flags → bitmask (an array of 31-bit words past 31 names),
  union → `[tag, ...branch fields]`; sparse → `[mask, ...present]` per 31 fields; collections as
  rows, `flat` or `columns`; set → array, map → `[k0, v0, …]`; delta → first value and
  differences; intern → `[table, body]` with strings as table indexes. The wire and canonical
  form are unchanged from 1.x
- Options: `codegen`, `validate` (boolean: the wire on decode), `sparse: true | paths`,
  `layout: layout | { path: layout }`, `intern: true | paths`, `delta: paths`, `stringify`,
  `fingerprint`, `maxDepth` (levels of a recursion; default: the call stack), `references`,
  `types` (wire types of custom types), `entity`, `entities`,
  `metaschema`, `compiled`; paths as errors spell them: `address.city`, `orders[].sku`, `scores{}`,
  `pair[1]`, `''`
- Schema evolution: append fields at the end, never reorder; older and newer versions interoperate;
  `schema.id` fingerprints the schema's signature (its canonical form plus the entities it
  references; FNV-1a 32-bit by default, `fingerprint: 'fnv1a64'` for a registry of many schemas,
  or a function); `compatible(previous, next)` (`/evolve`) names every evolution rule a newer
  version breaks, with a severity (error, warning, info) and a path; `baseline`/`restore` and the
  commands `protoarray snapshot <module>` and `protoarray check <module> --against <baseline>`
  hold a module to the schemas that shipped in CI (exit codes 0 compatible, 1 incompatible, 2 a
  wrong command line, 3 the module or the baseline could not be used); `resolve(writer, reader)`
  (`/resolve`) reads and writes another version by name (aliases, renames, widening);
  `SchemaRegistry` (`/registry`) keeps schemas by id and wraps payloads `[id, payload]`
- Binary wire (`/binary`): `toBinary(schema, value)` and `fromBinary(schema, bytes)` put the same
  schema on bytes (a header of presence bits per record, zigzag varints, float64, UTF-8 strings up
  to 21 characters and UTF-16 past them); both sides need the same schema, or one from `resolve`;
  the structure of a message is checked whatever `validate` says and a `DecodeError` carries
  `offset`; `intern`, `delta` and the `flat`/`columns` layouts have no binary form; a standalone
  module written with `--binary` carries the codec; over a round trip ahead of the text wire on
  every payload of the comparison (×1.1 on one record and long strings to ×6 on 32 doubles),
  ×1.6 encode and ×2.1 decode against JSON on one record, and fewer bytes on every payload but
  long strings (https://protoarray.vercel.app/guide/binary)
- Two backends: generated code (`new Function`) by default, composed closures where code
  generation is blocked (CSP without unsafe-eval, Cloudflare Workers, Vercel Edge); standalone
  modules (`/standalone`, `protoarray compile`) carry generated code and snapshots to such
  runtimes, without metaschema
- Streaming: `encodeEach`/`decodeEach` in the core; NDJSON, `TransformStream`s and the items of a
  large JSON array read as they arrive in `/stream`, a line or an item held at most `maxLength`
  characters (16 MiB by default)
- Validation: `validate: true` (default) checks the wire on decode; encode trusts its values, which
  metaschema's `check` and `parse` validate (`schema.source` is the metaschema Schema);
  `EncodeError` and `DecodeError` with `code`, `path` (`orders[1].sku`) and `schema`;
  `SchemaDefinitionError` for a snapshot or options protoarray cannot read
- Exports: `Schema`, `encode`, `decode`, `stringify`, `parse`, `encodeEach`, `decodeEach`,
  `SchemaDefinitionError`, `EncodeError`, `DecodeError`
- Upgrading from 1.x: https://protoarray.vercel.app/guide/migrating-from-1
- wrpc: a union of wrpc's packet types makes a packet codec (https://protoarray.vercel.app/guide/wrpc)
- Compared feature by feature with 22 serialization libraries (Protocol Buffers, Avro, Thrift,
  FlatBuffers, Cap'n Proto, MessagePack, CBOR, BSON, typed JSON):
  https://protoarray.vercel.app/guide/comparison
- Architecture (source → plan → backend → codec): https://protoarray.vercel.app/guide/architecture
- Docs: https://protoarray.vercel.app/ (guide, wire format, benchmarks, API reference)
